judgment.observations: The reconstruction captures the bunk-room layout, timber framing, central wooden cupboard, and right-side fireplace, but differs noticeably in proportions and appearance. The nearest left bunk fills more of the frame, with its front posts lower and farther right; the reference has more open foreground floor. Ceiling beams and wall timbers follow different patterns. The cupboard is smaller and closed, losing the reference’s open hanging compartment. The fireplace opening is smaller and more regularly bricked, with a flatter, paler surround. Bedding lacks the reference’s pillows, folds, and blue edging; bed frames appear thinner and less reflective. The right-edge bunk is replaced visually by a broad wooden panel with limited metal framing. Floorboards are lighter, more uniform, and less worn, while walls and ceiling lack much of the reference’s staining and peeling. Floor contacts are generally visible, but the render’s grain and diffuse shadows weaken their definition.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The foreground bunk appears larger or closer to the camera, and the room may appear narrower, but camera position and perspective could explain these differences. The cupboard appears shallower and the hearth less raised; these are uncertain depth impressions. Visible bed legs approach the floor plausibly, though exact contact and support cannot be established from the images.
